objective.statement: Learn seven small Italian words that join with other words to make a direction.
successCriteria: I know a and alla can mean “in the style of”, and con means with.
I know e means and, ma means but, non means not and senza means without.
I can work out a short direction such as alla marcia.

explanation.text: Many directions are built from small Italian helper words. On their own they do not say how fast or how loudly to play: they join other words together. You will meet these seven again and again.
“a” means at, to, by or in the style of. “al, alla” means to the, or in the manner of. “con, col” means with. “e, ed” means and.
“ma” means but. “non” means not. “senza” means without.
Helper words build directions. Alla marcia means in the style of a march. A tempo means go back to the speed from before. When you see a helper word, read the whole direction one word at a time.

music.textAlternative: A two-bar melody in G major marked a tempo.

explanation.caption: The words a tempo above a bar: go back to the speed from before.

explanation.text: con = with and senza = without are opposites. e = and, ma = but, non = not. a and alla both point to a style or manner.

music.textAlternative: A two-bar melody in G major marked alla marcia.

steps: Look at the words above the first bar: alla marcia.
Alla means in the style of, and marcia means march, so the player should sound like a march.
The words do not change the notes. They change the way the notes are played.

recap: A, alla, con, e, ma, non and senza are small helper words.
Con means with and senza means without; e means and, ma means but, non means not.
Read a direction one word at a time.
